knowledge:
- key_parameters: batchFactor=Either a vector or a factor indicating the batch each input matrix belongs to (use NULL if batch is unknown and only noise reduction is needed) ;; experimentalDesign=A list indicating the experimental conditions for each sample in each batch (must be consistent across batches) ;; Interaction=Logical indicating whether to model the interaction between experimental factors and batch factors (default is FALSE; setting to TRUE can improve correction but may dilute biological signal) ;; Variability=Minimum percent of data variability (0 to 1) that must be explained by each ARSyN model (default is 0.90) ;; beta=Numeric threshold where components representing more than beta times the average residual variability are identified as systematic noise and removed (default is 2) ;; test.comp=Maximum number of components allowed for PLS models (defaults to the minimal effective rank of the matrices if NULL)
- alternatives: ARSyN=The original method combining ANOVA and PCA for identifying and removing systematic noise in multifactorial designs, which ARSyNbac adapts for batch correction.
- when_to_use: Use when combining high-throughput omic datasets (such as transcriptomics, metabolomics, proteomics) from different laboratories, batches, or time points where batch effects are confounded with omic type effects. For multi-omic correction, at least one common omic data type must be shared across all batches.
- pitfalls: Confounding=The experimental design must not be completely confounded with batch effects (treatments must be represented across batches) ;; Feature identifiers=Common omics must use identical row names/identifiers across batches (e.g., do not mix Ensembl and RefSeq IDs) ;; Sample ordering=Within the same batch, different omic matrices must have the same samples in the exact same order ;; Batch effect magnitude=MultiBaC performance decreases at very high batch effect magnitudes, whereas ARSyN is less affected.

workflows.name: single_omic_correction
workflows.intent: Correct batch effects and reduce systematic noise in a single-omic dataset across multiple batches.
input: A.rna (matrix of gene expression for batch A)
B.rna (matrix of gene expression for batch B)
C.rna (matrix of gene expression for batch C)
workflows.stages: 1. Create the mbac S3 object using createMbac ;; 2. Run batch correction and/or noise reduction using ARSyNbac ;; 3. Plot the corrected data using the plot method
workflows.code:
data_RNA <- createMbac (inputOmics = list(A.rna, B.rna, C.rna), 
                    batchFactor = c("A", "B", "C"),
                    experimentalDesign = list("A" =  c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                                "Glu+", "Glu-", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-"),
                                       "B" = c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-"),
                                       "C" = c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-")),
                    omicNames = "RNA")

arsyn_1 <- ARSyNbac(data_RNA, modelName = "RNA", Variability = 0.95, 
                 batchEstimation = TRUE, filterNoise = FALSE, Interaction = FALSE)

plot(arsyn_1, typeP="pca.cor", bty = "L",
     pch = custom_pch, cex = 3, col.per.group = custom_col,
     legend.text = c("Color: Batch", names(data_RNA$ListOfBatches),
                     "Fill: Cond.", unique(colData(data_RNA$ListOfBatches$A)$tfactor)),
     args.legend = list("x" = "topright",
                        "pch" = c(NA, 15, 15, 15, 
                                  NA, 15, 0),
                        "col" = c(NA, "brown2", "dodgerblue", "forestgreen",
                                  NA, 1, 1),
                        "bty" = "n",
                        "cex" = 1.2))

workflows.name: multi_omic_correction
workflows.intent: Correct batch effects across multi-omic datasets distributed across different batches using a common omic.
input: A.rna (matrix of RNA for batch A)
A.gro (matrix of GRO for batch A)
B.rna (matrix of RNA for batch B)
B.ribo (matrix of RIBO for batch B)
C.rna (matrix of RNA for batch C)
C.par (matrix of PAR for batch C)
workflows.stages: 1. Create the multi-omic mbac object using createMbac ;; 2. Run the MultiBaC wrapper function to fit PLS models, predict missing omics, and perform batch correction ;; 3. Alternatively, run step-by-step using genModelList, genMissingOmics, and batchCorrection ;; 4. Visualize results using the plot method
workflows.code:
my_mbac <- createMbac (inputOmics = list(A.rna, A.gro, 
                                               B.rna, B.ribo, 
                                               C.rna, C.par), 
                    batchFactor = c("A", "A", 
                                    "B", "B", 
                                    "C", "C"),
                    experimentalDesign = list("A" =  c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                                "Glu+", "Glu-", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-"),
                                       "B" = c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-"),
                                       "C" = c("Glu+", "Glu+", 
                                               "Glu-", "Glu-")),
                    omicNames = c("RNA", "GRO", 
                                  "RNA", "RIBO", 
                                  "RNA", "PAR"))

my_final_mbac <- MultiBaC (my_mbac,
          				test.comp = NULL, scale = FALSE, 
          				center = TRUE, crossval = NULL, 
          				Interaction = TRUE,
          				Variability = 0.9,
          				showplot = TRUE,
          				showinfo = TRUE)

my_mbac_2 <- genModelList (my_mbac, test.comp = NULL, 
              			  scale = FALSE, center = TRUE,
              			  crossval = NULL,
              			  showinfo = TRUE)

multiBatchDesign <- genMissingOmics(my_mbac_2)

my_finalwise_mbac <- batchCorrection(my_mbac_2, 
                                     multiBatchDesign = multiBatchDesign,
                                     Interaction = TRUE,
                                     Variability = 0.90)

plot (my_final_mbac, typeP = "inner", comp2plot = c(1,2))
plot (my_final_mbac, typeP = "batch")
plot (my_final_mbac, typeP = "pca.org",
      cex.axis = 1, cex.lab = 1, cex = 3, bty = "L", 
      cex.main = 1.2, pch = 19)
plot (my_final_mbac, typeP = "pca.cor", 
      cex.axis = 1, cex.lab = 1, cex = 3, bty = "L", 
      cex.main = 1.2, pch = 19)
